question: Should OpenClaw expose Discord bot presence mutation to plugins as a public runtime API, and what gate, account scoping, audit/error behavior, and precedence model should it use?
rationale: The current implementation already has internal presence mutation paths, but promoting one to plugin runtime changes the public plugin contract and stored Discord bot-token control boundary.

options.title: Approve a gated Discord runtime API
options.body: Add a narrow Discord-owned `updatePresence`-style runtime seam with explicit gating, account selection, docs, tests, and precedence rules.

options.title: Keep presence as message action only
options.body: Keep dynamic presence limited to the existing default-off `setPresence` message action and document that plugins should not mutate Discord presence directly.

options.title: Fold into self-profile direction
options.body: Defer this to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/34004 if maintainers want one Discord identity/profile API instead of a separate presence-only plugin API.

recommendation.title: Approve a gated Discord runtime API
recommendation.body: Add a narrow Discord-owned `updatePresence`-style runtime seam with explicit gating, account selection, docs, tests, and precedence rules.

likelyOwner.reason: The main unresolved decision is whether to reintroduce a plugin-specific runtime seam after the plugin-runtime boundary refactor.
